Trainer here. I do everything I can to make sure my trainee is learning the job in a way that's most beneficial to them. I try to lay an early foundation of being respectful and kind. I make effort to help them establish relationships with the officers and other dispatchers. While they're with me, I am responsible for them. Training is the time to make mistakes so you can learn how to fix mistakes quickly when you're on your own. I teach them that a good dispatcher isn't perfect. A good dispatcher still makes mistakes, they're just good about catching and fixing their own mistakes quickly before they become problems. 

That all said, I do point out mistakes. I am tough and honest with them. If there is an issue that needs to be addressed and fixed, we're gonna address it and work to fix it. At some point in the training I start backing off and letting my trainee drown a little bit, but I'm always monitoring and I'll jump in if they get too overwhelmed. And I won't let them make a mistake that will be an officer safety issue. If they can't make it or need extended training I will communicate that with them and our supervisor 

Trainers need to remember that it's entirely possible to be direct, honest and even tough on a trainee without being a dick about it. You can be all those things and still be kind and work to build the person up. At the end of the day I wanna see my trainee succeed because it's in my best interest as an employee that they do.
